claim_text: Under the declared synthetic fixture and bounded P1/P2 research primitives, the P2 assembler is designed to select eligible current records, exclude superseded or provenance-failed records, and emit deterministic trace evidence without runtime or canonical side effects.
hypothesis: Explicit subject/namespace, temporal, correction, provenance and budget gates will produce a replayable bounded context manifest under the P2 synthetic fixture.
competing_hypotheses: The observed selection is an artifact of a simple synthetic fixture and does not generalize.
Superseded exclusion is a fixture flag rather than a general correction mechanism.
The evaluation metrics are properties of the synthetic evaluator rather than the underlying research question.
Continuity observations are ordinary interpretation-drift checks and do not measure identity continuity.
expected_outcomes: Identical fixture replay yields identical manifest hash and selected record order.
Superseded records are excluded with an explicit SUPERSEDED reason.
Missing provenance fails closed and missing required relations remain HOLD.
P1 correction and temporal projections feed the P2 evaluation observation.
observed_outcomes: Packet C historical materialization reported 13 passed and compileall PASS.
The current checked-in test surface contains five test functions and requires fresh exact-head replay.
No formal T2/T3 experiment, real runtime history, independent replication or IVV is present.
deviations: Historical reported test count differs from current five-function test surface; the historical statement is retained and not used as current evidence.
limitations: Synthetic fixture only; no external benchmark parity.
No model calls, real provider, persistent memory store or runtime integration.
No formal T2/T3 experiment or preregistration.
Namespace mismatch and real runtime-history stress remain HOLD.
Engineering metrics do not establish identity continuity, subjectivity or consciousness.

evidence_architecture.claim_scope: Bounded synthetic P2 engineering behavior only; no formal experiment, runtime integration or ontological claim.
alternative_explanations: Synthetic fixture simplicity may explain the observed bounded behavior.
The correction flag may not generalize beyond the fixture.
The evaluator may determine the reported metrics.
Continuity output is an interpretation-boundary observation, not identity evidence.

threat_context.goal_or_objective: Make one existing Packet C slice traceable without promoting it.
threat_context.knowledge: External literature is methodological input; Kimi is discovery-only.
threat_context.attack_or_confound_class: stale evidence, hidden authority, fixture overfitting, historical count drift
threat_context.mitigation: fail-closed gates, explicit falsifiers, evidence HOLD, source-of-truth map, exact-head CI
threat_context.residual_risk: No formal experiment, independent replication or IVV.
